questions.q: What asset category and cost center is FA-10452 incorrectly capitalized into?
questions.explain: FA-10452 is capitalized into Office Equipment (5-year life) and cost center 410 (Assembly), both incorrect for a CNC lathe physically located in Fabrication.

questions.q: What should FA-10452's correct category and cost center be?
questions.explain: A CNC lathe belongs in the Manufacturing Equipment — Machinery category (10-year life) and the Fabrication cost center (420), where it physically sits.

questions.q: Why does Derek Shaw make this categorization mistake?
options: Oracle Fusion forced the wrong category by default
He worked from a capital spending list sorted by approval date and carried forward the row above, a different asset
LTV has no Manufacturing Equipment category configured
questions.explain: Working from a worksheet organized by approval date rather than asset type, Derek carries the category and cost center forward from a different, unrelated asset row.

questions.q: Why does capitalizing FA-10452 with the wrong category not produce any system error or warning?
options: Oracle Fusion does not validate asset categories at all
Both Office Equipment and cost center 410 are independently valid values — the system has no way to know they're wrong for this specific asset
The asset was capitalized in draft mode only
Fixed Assets ignores category selection for CNC equipment
questions.explain: Office Equipment and cost center 410 are both legitimate, valid configuration values — the error is a functional/business judgment the system can't independently verify.

questions.q: What does this lesson say the miscategorization sets up for lesson 15?
options: A precise, calculable difference in January depreciation expense
An automatic reversal of the asset capitalization
questions.explain: Because Office Equipment depreciates over 5 years instead of Manufacturing Equipment's 10, lesson 15's depreciation run produces an exact, calculable overstatement.
